rationale: B is more decision-useful because it better distinguishes when each option is appropriate, especially the key caveat that full complexity may be necessary for behavioral reforms. It gives clearer implementation guidance, governance triggers, and review checkpoints. Its uncertainty handling is stronger: failure modes, disconfirming evidence, and conditions under which the recommendation would change. Quantitatively, B ties estimates to outside-view reference classes and provides more interpretable burden units. A is solid and concise, but its thresholds and forecasts feel more asserted than grounded, and its hybrid option depends heavily on automation without enough operational detail.
